title: The robots.txt Guide for AI Crawlers: Allow the Right Bots
dek: A copy-paste robots.txt that welcomes the AI crawlers you want citing you — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and more.
keywords: robots.txt, AI crawlers, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended

sections.h: Why robots.txt matters for AI visibility
p: robots.txt is the first gate every crawler checks. If an AI user-agent is disallowed — or just ambiguous — that engine may never read or cite your content.
Being explicit signals intent and maximizes coverage across AI surfaces.
Allow the major AI user-agents and point to your sitemap:
sections.code:
User-agent: *
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml

p: If you want AI citations, allow these bots. If you want to keep content out of AI training, disallow specific agents — but know that blocking them removes you from those engines' answers entirely.

faq.q: Which AI bots should I allow in robots.txt?
faq.a: To be cited, allow GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended, and link your sitemap.

faq.q: Does blocking GPTBot remove me from ChatGPT?
faq.a: Blocking GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot prevents OpenAI from indexing or citing your content in ChatGPT's answers. Only block if you intend to opt out.

faq.q: Where does robots.txt go?
faq.a: At your domain root: https://yourdomain.com/robots.txt. Add explicit per-user-agent Allow rules for the AI crawlers you want.

title: GEO for SaaS: How to Get Your Product Recommended by AI
dek: When buyers ask AI "what's the best tool for X", SaaS products with clear entities and structured proof win. Here's the GEO playbook for SaaS.
keywords: SaaS GEO, AI product recommendations, software AI citations, SaaS SEO

sections.h: AI is the new software shortlist
p: Buyers increasingly ask AI to compare and recommend tools before they ever visit a vendor site. If AI can't clearly understand what your product does and who it's for, you're left off the shortlist.
State plainly what category you're in, who it's for and what problem you solve — in your hero, your About page and your llms.txt. Add Organization and Product/SoftwareApplication schema.
Vague positioning ("the platform for modern teams") gives AI nothing to match a query against.
Surface comparisons, integrations, pricing and reviews as real HTML (and AggregateRating schema). These are exactly the facts AI needs to recommend you with confidence.

faq.q: How do I get my SaaS recommended by AI?
faq.a: Define a clear product entity (category, audience, problem) in copy, schema and llms.txt, and provide structured proof — comparisons, pricing and reviews — as crawlable HTML.

faq.q: What schema should a SaaS site use?
faq.a: Organization plus SoftwareApplication or Product, FAQPage for common questions, and AggregateRating for reviews.

faq.q: Why isn't my SaaS mentioned by AI?
faq.a: Usually vague positioning and thin structured data. Make your category and audience explicit and back claims with crawlable, marked-up facts.

title: How to Measure Your AI Visibility: The KPIs That Matter
dek: You can't improve what you don't measure. Here are the practical KPIs for AI visibility — from your GeoPageScan score to real AI-citation tracking.
keywords: measure AI visibility, AI visibility KPI, GEO metrics, AI citation tracking

p: A single 0–100 score across GEO/AEO/SEO categories — like the one GeoPageScan produces — gives you a baseline and a trend to manage. Re-scan after each change to measure the lift.

Periodically ask the major engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) the questions your customers ask, and record whether — and how — you're cited. Watch your referral analytics for AI sources too.
Track the signals that drive visibility: llms.txt present, schema coverage, AI bots allowed, and the share of pages with answer-first content. These move before citations do.

faq.q: How do I measure AI visibility?
faq.a: Use an AI-visibility score (0–100) as your baseline, track real citations by querying the major AI engines for your key questions, and monitor inputs like schema coverage and crawler access.

faq.q: What's a good AI-visibility KPI?
faq.a: The overall score tracked over time, the number of resolved critical/high findings, and the count of AI citations for your priority queries.

faq.q: How often should I check?
faq.a: Re-scan after each fix to confirm the lift, and review citations and score monthly as the AI landscape shifts.

title: How to Add FAQ Schema: A Step-by-Step Guide (with Examples)
dek: FAQPage schema is the most-quoted markup in AI answers. Here's exactly how to add it — with copy-paste JSON-LD and the mistakes to avoid.
keywords: FAQ schema, FAQPage, JSON-LD, how to add FAQ schema, AEO

sections.h: Why FAQPage schema is worth it
p: FAQPage markup explicitly maps questions to answers — exactly the structure AI engines lift into responses and the format Google uses for rich results. It's high-impact and quick to add.
Place this in your page <head>, with the questions and answers matching your visible content:
sections.code:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [{
    "@type": "Question",
    "name": "What is llms.txt?",
    "acceptedAnswer": { "@type": "Answer",
      "text": "A markdown file at your domain root that summarizes your site for AI." }
  }]
}
</script>

p: The schema answers must match what's visible on the page, every Question needs exactly one acceptedAnswer, and you should validate with Google's Rich Results Test before shipping.

comparison.title: FAQ schema: do vs don't
rows: Mark up hidden or fake questions

faq.q: How do I add FAQ schema?
faq.a: Add a FAQPage JSON-LD script to your page head with Question/acceptedAnswer pairs that match your visible FAQ, then validate with Google's Rich Results Test.

faq.q: Does FAQ schema help with AI?
faq.a: Yes — FAQPage is one of the most-quoted schema types in AI answers because it maps questions directly to answers.

faq.q: Can I fake questions in FAQ schema?
faq.a: No. The schema must match visible content; mismatched or hidden Q&A can be ignored or penalized. Mark up only real, visible FAQs.

title: A Zero-Click Content Strategy That Still Wins
dek: Zero-click search isn't the enemy — it's a branding and authority channel. Here's how to win even when users don't click.
keywords: zero-click search, AEO strategy, brand visibility, AI answers

p: When AI answers without a click, being the cited source still builds brand recognition and authority at the moment of intent. Visibility itself has value.

sections.h: Give a reason to click anyway
p: Lead with the answer for the citation, but offer depth the summary can't replace — tools, original data, examples — so motivated users still visit.
Track citations, branded search lift and assisted conversions, not just direct sessions, to see the real impact of AI visibility.

faq.q: Is zero-click search bad for my site?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Being the cited source builds brand authority at the moment of intent, and you can still earn clicks with depth the summary can't replace.

faq.q: How do I win in a zero-click world?
faq.a: Provide the concise answer for the citation plus unique depth, tools or data that give users a reason to click through.

faq.q: How do I measure zero-click impact?
faq.a: Track AI citations, branded search lift and assisted conversions, not just direct sessions.

title: Content Pruning: Cut the Pages Dragging Down Your Authority
dek: Thin, outdated pages dilute your topical authority for both Google and AI. Here's how to prune safely and strengthen the rest.
keywords: content pruning, thin content, topical authority, content audit, SEO

p: Low-quality, outdated or redundant pages dilute the signals that define your expertise. Removing or consolidating them concentrates authority on the pages that matter.
Audit pages by value and traffic, then update, consolidate or redirect the weak ones. Never delete without redirecting if a URL has links or history.
Merge thin posts into comprehensive ones, refresh facts and dates, and re-link them into your topic clusters.

faq.q: What is content pruning?
faq.a: Auditing and removing, consolidating or improving low-value pages so your strongest content carries more topical authority.

faq.q: Does pruning help AI visibility?
faq.a: Yes — concentrating quality signals on fewer, stronger pages makes your expertise clearer to AI and search.

faq.q: Should I delete old pages?
faq.a: Only after redirecting URLs with links or history. Prefer updating or consolidating over outright deletion.

title: JavaScript Rendering and Why AI Crawlers Skip Your Site
dek: Many AI crawlers don't run JavaScript. If your content only appears after JS, you may be invisible. Here's how to fix it.
keywords: JavaScript rendering, SSR, AI crawlers, crawlability, hydration

p: Unlike Googlebot, many AI crawlers fetch raw HTML and don't execute JavaScript. If your text, links or schema only appear after client-side rendering, those crawlers see an empty shell.
Use server-side rendering or static generation so your key content, headings and JSON-LD are present in the initial HTML response, not injected later by JS.
Check your page's raw HTML (view source or curl) — if the main content isn't there, neither AI crawlers nor your audit will see it.

faq.q: Do AI crawlers run JavaScript?
faq.a: Many don't. They fetch raw HTML, so content that only appears after client-side JS rendering can be invisible to them.

faq.q: How do I fix JS-only content?
faq.a: Use server-side rendering or static generation so key content and schema are in the initial HTML response.

faq.q: How do I check what crawlers see?
faq.a: View the page source or curl the URL — if the main content and JSON-LD aren't in the raw HTML, crawlers likely can't read them.
